title: O que é o microbioma? De palavra da moda a motor biológico
summary: A palavra microbioma está em toda parte, de palcos de conferências a podcasts de saúde. Mas muitas vezes é mal compreendida. Em termos estritos, microbioma é o ecossistema formado por uma comunidade coletiva de microrganismos... The post O que é o microbioma? De palavra da moda a motor biológico appeared first on IFF .
body_text: A palavra microbioma está em toda parte, de palcos de conferências a podcasts de saúde. Mas muitas vezes é mal compreendida. Em termos estritos, microbioma é o ecossistema formado por uma comunidade coletiva de microrganismos — incluindo bactérias, vírus, fungos e arqueas — juntamente com seu material genético, que habita um ambiente específico. No uso comum, porém, o termo geralmente se refere ao conjunto de comunidades microbianas e seu material genético que vivem no e sobre o corpo humano. É isso o que é o microbioma . O microbioma intestinal humano, por si só, abriga trilhões de microrganismos — aproximadamente o mesmo número de células humanas — com um repertório genético coletivo que supera o genoma humano em mais de 100 vezes. Esse vasto “segundo genoma” coordena processos fisiológicos diários muito além da digestão. Saiba mais sobre o microbioma humano Acesse O que é o microbioma? Não são apenas microrganismos A definição inclui não apenas os microrganismos em si, mas também toda a capacidade funcional codificada em seus genomas. Ou seja, não importa apenas quais microrganismos estão presentes, mas também o que eles fazem, ou seja, quais funções desempenham. Mas afinal, o que é o microbioma? O microbioma é o conjunto de ecossistemas que habitam praticamente todas as partes do corpo humano: intestino, pele, cavidade oral, olhos, trato respiratório, trato vaginal, entre outros. É um conjunto complexo de microrganismos que desempenham papéis essenciais na saúde metabólica, na saúde imune e na produção de nutrientes. Essas comunidades microbianas não apenas coexistem conosco: elas coevoluíram conosco e são fundamentais para a sobrevivência humana. Elas: Extraem energia de alimentos que seriam indigeríveis Produzem nutrientes essenciais, como vitamina K e vitaminas do complexo B Treinam e regulam o sistema imunológico Influenciam o cérebro via eixo intestino-cérebro (humor, estresse, cognição) Impactam a saúde metabólica e a integridade intestinal Para empresas que atuam no espaço de saúde, nutrição e bem-estar, esses insights biológicos são mais do que curiosidades científicas. Eles representam uma das fronteiras de inovação mais poderosas da próxima década. Para essas empresas, é isso que o microbioma significa. À medida que esse entendimento se aprofunda, a indústria de probióticos passa por sua própria revolução, evoluindo de listas genéricas de cepas para soluções precisas, direcionadas a mecanismos específicos. O microbioma produz nutrientes essenciais, fortalece e treina o sistema imunológico, modula a função cerebral e influencia a saúde metabólica. Além da lista de cepas: por que a função importa O mercado de probióticos é altamente competitivo, e muitos produtos ainda se baseiam apenas em listas de cepas com alegações genéricas. A ciência moderna do microbioma, no entanto, evoluiu de perguntas como “ O que é o microbioma? ” para “ O que essas cepas probióticas realmente fazem? ”. Essa abordagem funcional analisa a atividade metabólica dos microrganismos. Certas bactérias produzem metabólitos que interagem com o organismo e geram efeitos fisiológicos mensuráveis. À medida que a ciência se torna mais sofisticada, a validação funcional — e não apenas a identificação da cepa — se torna o principal indicador de qualidade. Esse avanço abre oportunidades relevantes para empresas que buscam diferenciação, como: Mecanismos de ação comprovados: Por exemplo, cepas específicas produzem ácidos graxos de cadeia curta que fortalecem a barreira intestinal e reduzem a inflamação. Alegações respaldadas por dados clínicos: Ensaios clínicos rigorosos em humanos que mensuram biomarcadores, e não apenas resultados autorrelatados. Narrativas científicas claras: Narrativa científica embasada em dados ômicos que demonstram interações em nível de vias metabólicas. Da associação à eficácia: um padrão mais elevado para a inovação do microbioma Durante anos, grande parte da pesquisa sobre o microbioma se concentrou em observações e na identificação de cepas microbianas encontradas em pessoas saudáveis. Naquela época, isso era tudo o que você precisava saber sobre o microbioma. Hoje, o padrão evoluiu para: Isolamento de cepas específicas Identificação de funções biológicas Mapeamento de metabólitos Testes em modelos controlados Essa abordagem rigorosa reduz os riscos para as marcas, melhora a reprodutibilidade e fortalece a narrativa do produto. A mudança não só atenua o escrutínio regulatório, como também constrói a confiança do consumidor em uma era de crescente demanda por bem-estar baseado em evidências. Veja como a pesquisa sobre probióticos fortalece a saúde. Acesse Como a IFF Health Sciences lidera essa transformação Em um mercado saturado de soluções genéricas, a IFF Health Sciences se destaca com expertise consolidada e com o portfólio HOWARU® clinicamente comprovado, com probióticos pioneiros de próxima geração (NGPs). Esses probióticos de próxima geração (NGPs) incluem microrganismos comensais (como Akkermansia ), que evoluíram junto aos humanos e permitem atuação mais direcionada em metabolismo, imunidade e outras funções. Para nossos parceiros comerciais, aproveitar a ciência do microbioma vai muito além do acesso a novas cepas. Não é mais disso que se trata o microbioma. Trata-se de adotar uma abordagem sistêmica que ofereça soluções cientificamente robustas, comercialmente escaláveis ​​e com diferenciação global. Microrganismos de nova geração A IFF Health Sciences lidera essa evolução por meio da plataforma de probióticos de próxima geração (NGP) e fluxos de trabalho avançados de descoberta. Estes apoiam a identificação e o desenvolvimento de cepas com funções específicas que visam mecanismos particulares, levando a indústria de associações genéricas à eficácia comprovada. Uma abordagem centrada na funcionalidade A IFF Health Sciences emprega métodos proprietários para identificar e isolar cepas com funções específicas, utilizando uma das maiores bibliotecas de cepas do setor e aproveitando a triagem de alto rendimento para isolar candidatos com foco na função. Essa seleção baseada na funcionalidade prioriza cepas com atividades metabólicas definidas e benefícios específicos para a saúde, reduzindo os prazos de desenvolvimento e aumentando a confiabilidade dos resultados em áreas como saúde metabólica, imunidade e integridade intestinal. Monitoramento das funções microbianas A bioinformática de alta resolução potencializa ainda mais esse processo, caracterizando a produção metabólica microbiana com detalhes excepcionais: mapeando genes, vias metabólicas e metabólitos-chave que impulsionam as interações com o hospedeiro. Essa visão baseada na genômica prevê e otimiza os efeitos fisiológicos, fornecendo narrativas transparentes e fundamentadas que ajudam os parceiros a construir alegações confiáveis ​​e a se destacar em um mercado competitivo. A abordagem da IFF Health Sciences, que prioriza a funcionalidade, foca em cepas com atividades metabólicas definidas e benefícios específicos para a saúde. Garantia de eficácia e segurança A IFF Health Sciences reduz os riscos da inovação conduzindo avaliações rigorosas em sistemas de modelos controlados, incluindo simulações in vitro e modelos pré-clínicos. Esses testes avaliam a eficácia, a segurança e a reprodutibilidade das cepas em condições biologicamente relevantes, identificando desafios precocemente e pavimentando um caminho mais claro para a validação clínica em humanos, elevando os padrões e garantindo a conformidade regulatória. Do laboratório ao mercado A capacidade de produção escalável da IFF Health Sciences permite fechar o ciclo, desde a concepção em laboratório até a comercialização global. Aproveitando tecnologias avançadas de fermentação, encapsulamento e formulação, além de programas abrangentes de estabilidade e fabricação, fornecemos soluções probióticas e de produtos naturais (NGPs) consistentes, de alta qualidade e com longa vida útil, prontas para atender às demandas do mercado. Um ecossistema de suporte Esta plataforma integrada permite que as marcas lancem produtos excepcionais, respaldados por ciência orientada por mecanismos. Nossos parceiros obtêm não apenas ingredientes inovadores, mas também um ecossistema completo de suporte que promete acelerar o tempo de lançamento no mercado, fortalecer o posicionamento competitivo e capturar o crescimento no cenário em constante evolução da saúde e nutrição. Este ecossistema completo, que combina linhas de pesquisa e desenvolvimento, conhecimento regulatório e expertise em formulação, capacita os parceiros da IFF Health Sciences a reduzir o risco de lançamentos, acelerar a entrada no mercado e conquistar um posicionamento premium em saúde metabólica, imunidade e categorias emergentes, como suporte ao eixo intestino-cérebro. A parceria com a IFF Health Sciences pode ajudar as marcas a impulsionar a inovação baseada no microbioma, transformando ciência de ponta em valor comercial mensurável. Trabalhe com a IFF Health Sciences para impulsionar a inovação no microbioma. Acesse Como será a próxima geração de produtos baseados no microbioma? A ciência do microbioma evoluiu da biologia descritiva para a inovação de precisão. Organizações que adotam uma abordagem orientada por mecanismos liderarão a próxima década de desenvolvimento em saúde e nutrição. A inovação em probióticos e microbioma impulsionada pela ciência começa com a escolha do parceiro certo. Em uma década em que a inovação orientada por mecanismos diferenciará líderes de seguidores, a IFF Health Sciences oferece o histórico comprovado e o pipeline de produtos inovadores para ajudar sua marca a desbravar o futuro. Pronto para explorar as possibilidades? Conecte-se com a IFF Health Sciences para obter suporte especializado em desenvolvimento de probióticos, cepas de última geração e soluções completas de fabricação. O que é o microbioma e outras perguntas O que é o microbioma em termos científicos simples? O microbioma refere-se ao conjunto completo de microrganismos e de seu material genético que vivem no e sobre o corpo humano. Ele inclui bactérias, fungos e outros micróbios, bem como os genes que determinam sua atividade metabólica. Qual é a diferença entre microbioma e microbiota? Microbiota refere-se apenas aos próprios microrganismos. Isso não é o que é o microbioma. O microbioma refere-se a todo o habitat, incluindo os microrganismos (bactérias, arqueias, eucariotos inferiores e superiores, e vírus), seus genomas (genes) e as condições ambientais ao redor. Como o microbioma intestinal afeta a saúde metabólica? O microbioma intestinal produz metabólitos que influenciam a absorção de nutrientes, os sinais de saciedade, o movimento do intestino, a resposta do organismo à inflamação e outras vias de sinalização metabólica. Essas interações podem impactar a saúde metabólica e as respostas fisiológicas sistêmicas. Por que o mecanismo de ação ganhou relevância na pesquisa sobre microbioma? O mecanismo de ação demonstra como uma cepa específica produz efeitos mensuráveis por meio de vias biológicas bem definidas. Isso fortalece a validação clínica e sustenta alegações de saúde confiáveis. Como as cepas probióticas são validadas clinicamente? A validação clínica envolve uma série de testes, incluindo estudos in vitro e em animais, seguidos por ensaios clínicos em humanos para confirmar segurança, eficácia e reprodutibilidade. The post O que é o microbioma? De palavra da moda a motor biológico appeared first on IFF .

title: How to Optimize Tool Calling for AI Agents
summary: Optimize AI agent tool calling with better tool design, simpler schemas, atomic tools, dynamic filtering, and evals, not just a bigger model.
body_text: To optimize tool calling, improve the full path from user request to tool selection, input generation, and task completion. The biggest gains usually come from clearer tool descriptions, simpler schemas, atomic tools, dynamic tool filtering, model-and-harness testing, and ongoing evals rather than simply switching to a larger model.

title: POET Technologies Recaps Highlights of CEO’s Update on Commercial Activities and Provides Results of 2026 AGM
summary: Press release from POET Technologies posted on Jun 30, 2026
body_text: TORONTO, Ontario, June 30, 2026 –– POET Technologies Inc. (“POET” or the “Company”) (NASDAQ: POET), the designer and developer of Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs), light sources and optical modules for the AI and data center markets, today reported the voting results of its Annual General Meeting (the “AGM”), which was held virtually on Friday, June 26, 2026, and recapped highlights from the presentation given by Chairman & CEO Dr. Suresh Venkatesan. In his annual update to shareholders and analysts, Dr. Venkatesan delivered a robust report that punctuated the Company’s recent advancements in commercial activities and manufacturing deliverables. Key highlights of the presentation included: A reiteration that the Company’s production ramp is currently on schedule and expected to begin in the second half of 2026 with volume shipments of optical engines to customers. POET anticipates expanding capacity to meet demand of up to 1 million units per month by the end of 2027. This represents a more than 10x increase from current production capacity. After raising $830 million in equity capital in the past 12 months — with the potential to raise, if exercised, up to an additional $661 million through warrants — the Company plans an initial deployment of approximately $50 million for the purchase of capital equipment in the second half of 2026. The strength of the balance sheet facilitates POET’s efforts to secure supplies of critical components through long-term strategic partnerships with key suppliers, potentially increasing its ability to fulfill orders and neutralizing the threat posed by critical shortages of some materials. POET Blazar™, the Company’s cutting-edge hybrid laser for its external light source product designed to power high-bandwidth data communications in artificial intelligence (AI) networks and hyperscale data centers, is currently on schedule for expected deployment at scale in 2028. The Company has more than 10 active customer engagements that combined are expected to exceed $100 million in future annual revenue. These engagements include the recently announced agreement with Lumilens, a previously-announced production order for 800G optical engines and a significant NRE agreement for External Light Source (ELS) applications from a new customer. The Company intends to add approximately 50 more staff to its global workforce of 115 within the next few months. Dr. Venkatesan’s full video presentation, including the Q&A segment that followed his remarks, can be accessed through the Company’s website at: https://poet-technologies.com/videos . The presentation slides alone can be found on the “Shareholders Meeting (AGM)” page of the Investors section of the website: https://www.poet-technologies.com/investors . Prior to the CEO’s update, the Company’s Senior VP, Accounting and Finance, Kevin Barnes, delivered customary introductions and the call to order, and POET’s Chairman of the Compensation Committee, Glen Riley, conducted the formal business of the Meeting, which included the approval of all proposals outlined in the Company’s management information circular and voting material as previously distributed to shareholders. AGM Voting Results Summary A detailed Report on Voting Results of the AGM follows. In summary, the shareholders of the Company approved the following proposals: Re-election of Suresh Venkatesan, Jean-Louis Malinge, Theresa Lan Ende, Glen Riley, Sohail Khan and Robert “Bob” Tirva as directors, with no director receiving less than 94.35% of the votes cast; Appointment of Davidson & Company LLP as the Company’s auditors by 97% of the votes cast; Detailed Report of AGM Voting Results In accordance with section 11.3 of National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations , this report briefly describes the matters voted upon and the outcome of the votes at the annual general meeting of shareholders of POET Technologies Inc. (the " Company ") held virtually via the MEETNOW.GLOBAL platform on June 26, 2026 (the " Meeting "). Each of the matters is described in greater detail in the Company's management information circular dated May 1, 2026 (the " Circular ") 1. Election of Directors . Each of the nominees set for in the Circular were elected as directors to serve until the next annual meeting of shareholders, or until their respective successors are elected or appointed. The following table sets forth the vote of the shareholders at the Meeting with respect to the election of directors: 2. Appointment of Davidson & Company LLP . The Company's shareholders approved the appointment of Davidson & Company LLP as auditors of the Company to hold office until the close of the next annual meeting of shareholders of the Company at such remuneration as may be fixed by the directors of the Company. The following table sets forth the vote of the shareholders at the Meeting with respect to the appointment of Davidson & Company LLP: The Company had 172,590,000 issued and outstanding shares at the time of the meeting. Restricted Stock Units (“RSUs”) Following the AGM, the POET Board of Directors met to elect officers and to determine RSU grants for directors. For their service on the Board of Directors until the next Annual General Meeting, the five independent directors were granted a total of 79,450 RSUs, which will vest on the first anniversary of the grant. The cash portion of each director’s compensation is paid over four quarters. Both are paid in accordance with an established formula for director compensation. The RSUs were granted subject to provisions of the Company’s 2025 Omnibus Incentive Plan and are subject to the NASDAQ Exchange policies and applicable securities laws. For further details on the Company’s share capital, refer to the Company’s Financial Statements and MD&A for the three-months ended March 31, 2026, which may be found on SEDAR+ and EDGAR. About POET Technologies Inc. POET is a design and development company offering high-speed optical engines, light source products and custom optical modules to the artificial intelligence systems market and to hyperscale data centers. POET's photonic integration solutions are based on the POET Optical Interposer™, a novel, patented platform that allows the seamless integration of electronic and photonic devices into a single chip using advanced wafer-level semiconductor manufacturing techniques. POET's Optical Interposer-based products are lower cost, consume less power than comparable products, are smaller in size and are readily scalable to high production volumes. In addition to providing high-speed (800G, 1.6T and above) optical engines and optical modules for AI clusters and hyperscale data centers, POET has designed and produced novel light source products for chip-to-chip data communication within and between AI servers, the next frontier for solving bandwidth and latency problems in AI systems. POET's Optical Interposer platform also solves device integration challenges across a broad range of communication, computing and sensing applications. POET is headquartered in Toronto, Canada, with operations in Singapore, Penang, Malaysia and Shenzhen, China. More information about POET is available on our website at www.poet-technologies.com . title: The Claims Moment of Truth: Why Predictive Modeling Is No Longer Optional
body_text: Home Resources Resources Download Center Guidewire Conversations Podcasts Blog Help and Support Insurance Technology FAQ Blog Blog All Blog Posts Best Practices Careers Customer Viewpoint Developers General Interest Partner Perspective Technology Trends Industry Trends Technology The Claims Moment of Truth: Why Predictive Modeling Is No Longer Optional A bodily injury claim comes in on Monday morning. A routine rear-end collision involving soft-tissue neck and back pain, the kind of minor injury that typically resolves on its own in most files. Nothing about it trips a flag, so it lands in the general queue and waits its turn. Ninety days later, a lawyer has become involved and the estimated cost of the claim has more than tripled. A single runaway claim like this can quickly wipe out the margin of a hundred well-handled ones. This is the file that should worry a claims executive, precisely because nothing about it looked like trouble at intake. Expensive bodily injury claims rarely announce themselves on day one. By the time severity is visible in the file, the damage is already done. This highlights the fundamental blind spot in how most claims operations triage. They sort files by the severity observable at first notice of loss (FNOL), operating on the assumption that ultimate cost can be read off the intake data. The evidence points the other way. What a bodily injury claim finally costs depends far more on the path it takes after FNOL than on how it looks at intake, and that path is partly set by the insurer's own early handling decisions. The Insurance Research Council has studied attorney involvement in auto injury claims since the 1970s, and the pattern has held: represented bodily injury claimants settle for roughly 3.5 times what unrepresented claimants with comparable injuries receive, and represented claims account for about 85% of all dollars paid out under bodily injury (BI) coverage. The easy interpretation is that attorneys are drawn to claims that were destined to be expensive anyway. That is partly true, and for years it was hard to separate selection from cause. The more recent work closes that gap. A 2026 study in the Journal of Risk and Insurance , led by Bogdan Savych at the Workers Compensation Research Institute (WCRI), used an instrumental-variables design across more than 950,000 lost-time claims to isolate the effect of representation itself, and found that attorney involvement causally raises indemnity, independent of the underlying injury. The path a claim takes helps determine what it costs, which means some of that cost is still in play at the point an adjuster first touches the file. The same WCRI research program also looked at why injured workers hire attorneys in the first place, and the answer is rarely the injury. Workers who believed their claim was being denied or delayed retained counsel at around 34%, against roughly 5% among those who sensed no problem. The trigger was the experience of the claims process: whether a claim goes down the expensive path is, to a meaningful degree, a decision the insurer participates in during the first few weeks. The window for that influence is narrow: a 2025 Milliman analysis that ran natural-language processing across workers’ comp claim notes found that attorneys are identified on only about 8% of claims within two days of first report, while roughly 70% surface more than a month later, usually after a dispute over compensability or medical treatment is already underway. By the time representation appears in the file, the early handling friction that shaped it is months in the past. What Predictive Modeling Actually Does This is the gap predictive modeling is built to close, though it is rarely sold that way. The standard pitch is about efficiency, faster routing and lighter workloads, and those are real benefits. The true value of a model lies in its ability to flag, at first notice, which seemingly benign claims are tracking toward a high-cost path while adjusters still have time to intervene. What a good model adds is the ability to read combinations of data points. A short reporting delay means little by itself, and a soft-tissue injury is the most ordinary thing in the file. The same soft-tissue injury, reported late, in a jurisdiction where attorney involvement runs high, is a different matter altogether, and an experienced adjuster would read it as one. The model applies that reading to every file at first notice, not only the ones a senior adjuster happens to pull. That experience and intuition matter more every year, because the people who currently supply it are leaving the workforce. Drawing on Bureau of Labor Statistics data, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce projects that about half of insurance professionals aged 55 and older will retire by the early 2030s, opening a gap of more than 400,000 roles. A senior adjuster carries an internalized sense of how these complex claims resolve, assembled from thousands of outcomes, and that sense is exactly what flags the dangerous file early. A good predictive model captures this intuition and helps improve outcomes across the entire portfolio. Where This Lands in Practice None of this pays off without changing the way claims are triaged. Too often, a model is built and wired into an existing system where it produces a credible score, only to have the claim routed to the same queue to sit on the same timeline. As a result, the score becomes another ignored data field on a screen. A predictive score that changes no real-time decision is just an expensive form of reporting. The programs that produce results do the harder thing, which is to change the work that follows the score. High-propensity claims get a senior adjuster regardless of the dollar reserve, and they get a substantive outreach call inside the first day rather than a form letter in week three. That call is the intervention the WCRI data points to: the claimant's sense of whether the process is fair forms in exactly that window, and it is the strongest lever the carrier has before an attorney is ever involved. What a bodily injury claim will ultimately cost takes shape over the months after first notice, and the carrier has a hand in shaping it. The carriers that organize around that insight, and use a predictive model to find the files where their hand still matters, are the ones that will keep pulling away from the field. The rest will continue sorting claims by how they look on day one, only to be surprised by what those claims eventually become. Sources Insurance Research Council, Attorney Involvement in Auto Injury Claims (2014). Savych, B., et al. "Unresolved conflict in workers' compensation: The impact of legal representation on workers' compensation benefits." Journal of Risk and Insurance (2026). Milliman IntelliScript, "How does attorney involvement impact workers' compensation claims?" (2025). U.S. Chamber of Commerce, The America Works Report: Industry Perspectives . title: The 3 P.M. Slump Is Not Laziness; It Could Be The Air You’re Breathing
summary: Stale workplace air can be an invisible energy thief—and how data can help us reclaim our afternoon focus The clock ticks to 3 p.m., and suddenly, a collective heavy fog rolls over the workplace. You stare at your email like it’s hieroglyphics. Your motivation evaporates, and the temptation to crawl under the desk for a [...]
body_text: Stale workplace air can be an invisible energy thief—and how data can help us reclaim our afternoon focus The clock ticks to 3 p.m., and suddenly, a collective heavy fog rolls over the workplace. You stare at your email like it’s hieroglyphics. Your motivation evaporates, and the temptation to crawl under the desk for a quick nap, George Costanza-style, becomes overwhelmingly strong. It happens to me and I’ll bet it happens to you. It seems to be a universal office phenomenon. For years, we’ve blamed this mid-afternoon crash on personal failings: a late-night Hulu binge-watch, a sugar crash, or that extra slice of garlic bread with our lunchtime fettuccine alfredo. A quick skim through Reddit shows that theories abound, from stress to hormone levels. While our biological circadian rhythm does naturally dip twelve hours after our deepest sleep cycle, science points to another stealthy workplace culprit causing the afternoon slump: the very air we are breathing. The Invisible Energy Thief: Stale Office Air Throughout the workday, an invisible transformation occurs within enclosed meeting rooms and workspaces. As a group of people sits together hour after hour, they absorb oxygen and exhale carbon dioxide (CO 2 ). In modern, closed-door office buildings, this CO 2 has nowhere to go. While fresh outdoor air sits comfortably at around 400 parts per million (ppm) of C0 2 , a crowded conference room can easily spike past 1,000 to 2,500 ppm by mid-afternoon. Leading cognitive studies, including research from Exposure, Epidemiology, and Risk Program, Department of Environmental Health, Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, have shown that these elevated indoor CO 2 levels can impair human cognitive function. High carbon dioxide accumulation can induce brain fog, lethargy, headaches and a sense of sleepiness. Combine this with Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) from office furniture and stagnant, dry air from HVAC systems, and your workplace can become an incubator for fatigue. Unmasking the Problem You cannot fix a problem you cannot see. Because CO 2 and VOCs are odorless and invisible, teams usually realize the air quality has degraded only after they are already feeling exhausted. To combat this, forward-thinking organizations are turning to smart environmental tracking to make the invisible visible. Imagine an IT or facilities manager tracking room health metrics over time. By using wall-mounted environmental sensors like Logitech Spot , teams can continuously monitor indoor factors like carbon dioxide, dust, and aerosols that quietly drain employee concentration. This data takes the guesswork out of understanding exactly why focus plummets during the afternoon crash. But this smart sensor doesn’t work only in conference rooms. Environmental Sensing for Healthier Collaboration Spaces Managing air quality is especially crucial in high-stakes collaboration spaces where sustained focus is paramount. To bridge the gap between daily collaborative meetings and environmental awareness, modern hardware is building health tracking right into the room infrastructure. For example, when a team gathers around an all-in-one video collaboration board like the Logitech Rally Board 65 , the device does double duty. While facilitating hybrid communication, its integrated, built-in sensors silently track local room conditions. That information is sent into a dashboard for IT or Facilities teams to see, and if necessary, make changes to the space to help keep everyone awake, alert, and creative. Reclaiming The Afternoon The 3 p.m. slump doesn’t have to be an inevitable tax on workplace productivity. By understanding that afternoon fatigue is a mixture of human biology and environmental design, businesses can take proactive steps. Reclaiming your team’s focus requires moving beyond endless cups of coffee to looking at the infrastructure of the workspace itself. Armed with smart, data-driven solutions like Logitech Spot and Rally Board 65, companies can finally clear the air, banish the afternoon fog, and keep their workforce clear-headed and focused through the last, longest stretch of the day. Sources: ASHRAE Position Document on Indoor Carbon Dioxide (2025) CDC NIOSH Ventilation FAQ on CO₂ Monitoring Harvard/Allen et al. Cognitive Function and CO₂ Study Harvard Healthy Buildings Research on CO₂ and Cognitive Performance 2023 Meta-Analysis of Indoor CO₂ and Cognitive Performance

title: How omnichannel analytics in B2B drive visibility and operational control
summary: Master B2B omnichannel analytics: gain visibility across teams, tools, and conversations to reduce friction and scale operations effectively.
body_text: Master B2B omnichannel analytics: gain visibility across teams, tools, and conversations to reduce friction and scale operations effectively. Customer work in B2B rarely stays in one place. A request might start in email, shift to Slack, turn into a call, and end up buried in a CRM note. It passes through multiple teams and tools — and that’s where things get messy. Most analytics tools track activity by channel, so you see response times or ticket counts — but not where work slows, why a handoff stalls, or where communication breaks down. The impact is real: the typical B2B company spends nearly three hours coordinating for every hour spent solving customer problems. This isn’t a lack of effort, but a byproduct of growth. As B2B organizations scale , more people, tools, and processes get involved, and visibility suffers. Omnichannel analytics restores that visibility by tracing how customer conversations move across systems and workflows. With a full view of each customer request, B2B teams can measure end-to-end performance and deliver a better customer experience from first touch to final resolution. What omnichannel analytics means for B2B Omnichannel analytics is an integral part of B2B customer engagement. Instead of treating email, chat, and CRM activity as separate streams, omnichannel reporting tracks each request as it moves through different teams and systems. You see the full lifecycle of a conversation rather than isolated interactions. That’s what sets it apart from multichannel analytics , which looks at performance within each channel independently. An omnichannel approach gives teams a complete view of the customer journey across every touchpoint. With omnichannel data, you gain awareness of how requests move, where they slow, and where service-level agreement (SLA) risk starts to build. And the need for this insight is rising. As software ecosystems expand, tool-switching has grown from 24% to 39% , making it harder for B2B teams to stay aligned without a unified view. Where ticket-first analytics tools focus on managing queues, omnichannel analytics goes further by mapping how requests progress from one handoff to the next. It connects the entire journey and surfaces operational insight you can’t get from channel-level metrics. Why omnichannel analytics matters in B2B Customer requests constantly shift across multiple channels and teams before they’re resolved. Omnichannel analytics gives teams a clear view of this movement, making it easier to spot bottlenecks, maintain SLA compliance, and respond efficiently, even as complexity and volume rise. Here are the areas where omnichannel analytics adds the most value in B2B. Visibility across channels Omnichannel marketing analytics show where customers get stuck while purchasing or engaging with your brand. This clarity helps leaders prioritize fixes or adjust workflows, so requests move smoothly between teams. That’s how visibility drives better operational decisions — by pinpointing exactly where improvements will have the most impact. Ownership and accountability Bring clarity to accountability. Omnichannel analytics shows who owns each request, how long it takes to resolve, and whether SLA commitments are met. This information helps managers evaluate response quality and completion rates to identify gaps in ownership or training. Front’s Support Report surfaces these insights in one place, making it easier to monitor performance and route work to the appropriate owner. Operational resilience even under peak times Omnichannel analytics solutions show where operations strain under high demand. They highlight recurring customer issues, escalation trends, and response patterns that impact performance. With this omnichannel insight, teams can adjust staffing and refine workflows to stay consistent during volume spikes. An understanding of how processes hold up under pressure allows leaders to proactively prevent backlogs and keep service levels stable . See how Ridepanda kept their customer communications human with Front, handling 4x higher volume while achieving high CSAT scores. Insight into customer experience weak points Not every breakdown announces itself. Accounts quietly churn. Customers stop responding. And somewhere in the thread, a handoff lost the context that would’ve saved it. Omnichannel analytics makes those failure points visible before they compound. You can see where response times spike by channel, which handoffs consistently lose context, and where requests stall between teams — like when a billing dispute routes through support but needs sign-off from finance and account management. Patterns like these rarely show up on dashboards. They only become visible when you’re tracking the full thread, not just the last reply. That visibility is what separates proactive operations from reactive ones. When leaders can see where the customer experience degrades — not just that it did — they can fix the right thing. Key capabilities of omnichannel analytics platforms An effective omnichannel analytics platform gives you control across every workflow and handoff. In complex B2B environments, it shows the entire path of customer requests and flags risks early enough for teams to intervene. Here are the capabilities to look for when evaluating different platforms. Unified reporting Unified reporting brings data from email, chat, social media, and CRM into a single view of customer interactions. Rather than juggling disconnected sources or reconciling scattered reports, leaders can track how requests move through multiple channels and make decisions with full context for every conversation. Conversation-level analytics Ticket counts alone miss the nuances of the customer experience. Conversation-level analytics follow requests as they move between teams and tools, revealing where friction occurs and who owns each step. This clarity is even more critical with AI in the mix. Recent data shows that 71% of companies using AI experienced coordination failures in the past three months, with 24% saying that AI created extra work. Another 22% lost context during handoffs, and 20% failed to route requests correctly. With proper omnichannel analytics, teams can detect escalation patterns before they become systemic and ensure AI enhances — not disrupts — customer support workflows. SLA tracking Monitoring SLAs across teams and touchpoints keeps requests moving, regardless of which channel the request came through. Leaders gain a clear view of bottlenecks, enabling them to enforce accountability and take corrective action before delays affect customer relationships or revenue. See how TEquipment went from responding to customers in 8 hours to just 15 minutes with Front. Role-based dashboards Different teams have different North Star metrics. Quarters end, goals shift, and leadership expectations change. Custom dashboards provide real-time visibility and deliver the right metrics for each role, giving teams the exact data they need to act quickly and stay aligned without wading through irrelevant information. Trend detection Trend detection uncovers recurring issues and process gaps that can trigger escalations or slow resolution. With these insights, B2B managers can adjust staffing and workflows to improve customer service quality and stay ahead of complaints. Omnichannel analytics platform types When evaluating omnichannel analytics, it helps to understand the types of software that make these insights possible . Here are four common customer data platforms: Customer operations platforms: Centralize customer workflows, handoffs, and multichannel data so teams can track requests and preserve continuity. Customer support or help desk solutions: Manage and resolve tickets automatically while providing insight into response times and escalations. Data integration/BI tools: Consolidate data from disparate systems to uncover trends, measure performance, and inform operational decisions. Omnichannel reporting modules: Layer reporting across channels to show the full lifecycle of customer conversations and gauge workflow efficiency. How Front powers omnichannel analytics for B2B teams In B2B organizations, coordination isn’t just a function — it’s the work itself. Customer requests bounce between email, chat, and internal tools before getting resolved, making visibility critical to success. Omnichannel analytics tracks conversations end-to-end to show exactly where communication breaks down. Front gives leaders that clarity by mapping every touchpoint in the customer journey. Handoffs, roadblocks, and SLA risks become immediately visible, allowing you to take proactive action instead of reactive firefighting. Even under heavy volume, Front keeps teams aligned by maintaining clear ownership and ensuring requests move in the right direction — all without switching dashboards or chasing fragmented data. The results are tangible: faster resolution times, stronger accountability, and smoother cross-department collaboration. With greater insight and coordinated workflows, B2B leaders can scale confidently and resolve requests with ease. Explore how Front gives your team full visibility into conversation flow and optimizes operations on every channel. FAQ What challenges do companies face when implementing omnichannel analytics? Many companies struggle with fragmented systems, inconsistent data, and unclear ownership across teams, which makes it hard to get a complete view of customer conversations. They also face resistance to new workflows, requiring careful change management to make sure teams adopt omnichannel analytics effectively. How often should B2B teams review omnichannel analytics? B2B teams should review analytics regularly, ideally weekly or biweekly, to catch SLA risks and recurring issues before they escalate. Frequent reviews help managers fine-tune staffing, workflows, and priorities in real time to keep operational performance strong.

title: Cincinnati Financial Corporation Expands Board With Appointment of Independent Director
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Cincinnati Financial Corporation (Nasdaq: CINF) – Cincinnati Financial Corporation's board of directors added a 15th seat, appointing Lisa M....
body_text: CINCINNATI , June 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cincinnati Financial Corporation (Nasdaq: CINF ) – Cincinnati Financial Corporation's board of directors added a 15th seat, appointing Lisa M. Franchetti to the board and as a member of its audit committee, effective immediately. Admiral Franchetti retired from the U.S. Navy in 2025, after a nearly 40-year career marked by leadership at every operational level, culminating in her service as the 33rd Chief of Naval Operations from November 2023 to February 2025. As Chief of Naval Operations, Franchetti led a force of more than 600,000 personnel, advanced the Navy's strategic modernization and warfighting readiness initiatives, and focused on fleet growth, emerging technologies and workforce development. She is the first woman to hold the role and to serve on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. Prior to becoming the Navy's top officer, she served as Vice Chief of Naval Operations and as Director for Strategy, Plans and Policy on the Joint Staff. Her career also includes command of the destroyer USS Ross, Destroyer Squadron 21, two carrier strike groups, U.S. Naval Forces Korea and the U.S. Sixth Fleet, where she oversaw complex joint operations. Following her Navy career, she founded Franchetti Strategic Solutions LLC, a strategic consulting firm specializing in national security advising, global strategic planning and operational transformation strategies. Passionate about developing the next generation of leaders, she served as 2026 Fellow at the University of Chicago and will be a Distinguished Practitioner at Northwestern University in 2027. Franchetti holds a bachelor's degree from Northwestern University, a master's degree from the University of Phoenix and is a Distinguished Graduate of the Naval War College. Stephen M. Spray, president and chief executive officer, commented: "Lisa's extensive experience in strategic planning and leadership at the highest federal levels make her an ideal candidate for our board. I know she'll immediately bring a valuable perspective to board discussions as our directors work together to enhance the value we create for shareholders now and into the future." title: Synchrony's CareCredit Makes It Easy to Pay for Your Pet's Training, Boarding, Daycare and Grooming with Pet Resort Hospitality Group Partnership
summary: Key Highlights Pay with the CareCredit credit card at more places: CareCredit is now accepted at 40 Pet Resort Hospitality Group…...
body_text: Key Highlights Pay with the CareCredit credit card at more places : CareCredit is now accepted at 40 Pet Resort Hospitality Group locations in 12 states for training, boarding, daycare and grooming. Supporting pet care education : The partnership also supports Pet Resort University, an education program for pet care professionals—part of CareCredit's ongoing commitment to industry training. Helping pet owners manage costs : This partnership reinforces CareCredit's dedication to giving pet owners more flexible ways to pay for their pets' needs—from veterinary visits to everyday services beyond the vet. STAMFORD, Conn. , June 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Synchrony (NYSE: SYF), a premier consumer financial services company, today announced a new partnership with Pet Resort Hospitality Group (PRHG), an innovative leader in pet care services. This collaboration establishes the CareCredit credit card as the preferred financing solution for PRHG's network of premier pet resorts across 40 locations in 12 states, offering pet parents convenient options to manage costs for boarding, grooming and training services. It also supports education and growth opportunities for employees through the Pet Resort University education program, which empowers the industry, staff and partners to provide the best care possible to pets. Pet owners can use their CareCredit credit card at participating PRHG locations, including premier destinations like Paws 'n' Rec, Playtime Pet Resort and Olde Towne Pet Resort, to pay for comprehensive services such as daycare, professional grooming, overnight boarding, day camp packages and specialized training programs. With the rapidly growing pet grooming, daycare and lodging market projected to reach $10 billion to $13 billion,1 CareCredit is addressing this increased demand by helping to remove financial barriers to these essential services. "CareCredit's core mission is to enable pet parents to offer the best possible care for their cherished pets across every aspect of their lives, beyond just medical needs to hospitality experiences," said Jonathan Wainberg, Senior Vice President, General Manager, Pet, Synchrony. "This partnership with Pet Resort Hospitality Group allows us to expand our commitment to holistic pet well-being, offering families a clear and accessible way to budget for everything from a fun-filled day at a pet resort to essential grooming and training. We're also providing peace of mind by ensuring they receive high-quality care even when their parents can't be with them." Additionally, this partnership furthers education at Pet Resort University, PRHG's training program for its pet care professionals, partners and staff. Through this program, CareCredit is contributing to the continued learning that is necessary to provide the best care to all furry family members, empowering individuals in the pet industry through career-building opportunities. "Partnering with CareCredit allows us to build on the continued growth of our network and commitment to serving thousands of pets, parents and staff members each year," said Jason Duffy, CEO of PRHG. "Using the trusted CareCredit credit card can help remove financial barriers, ensuring more pet parents can access the high-quality services that contribute to a pet's overall happiness, mental stimulation and development we are passionate about providing. Additionally, the partnership will expand our education program to assist staff and partners in building their careers to provide care for pets across the country." In 2025, PRHG's extensive network served 71,000 pets belonging to 59,000 pet parents, facilitating 95,000 boarding stays and 5.1 million hours of daycare. The company employs more than 1,000 dedicated professionals, reflecting its significant presence and impact in the pet services industry. PRHG also partners with leading pet resorts to preserve their legacy and elevate their operations. This partnership is a continuation of Synchrony's ongoing efforts to enhance and expand its CareCredit health and wellness offerings to build a comprehensive ecosystem that supports pet health and financial well-being. For more than 35 years, CareCredit has provided a financing solution for veterinary services, treatments and diagnostics. The health and wellness credit card helps provide pet owners with access to a variety of financing options to ensure they are financially prepared to support their pets, within their budget. CareCredit is accepted at more than 27,000 veterinary practices and all public veterinary university hospitals in the U.S., to ensure pet owners can access necessary care for their pets, ranging from routine checkups and emergency surgeries to grooming and boarding. About Synchrony Synchrony (NYSE: SYF) is a leading consumer financing company that has been at the heart of American commerce and opportunity for nearly a century. Synchrony delivers credit and banking products that empower tens of millions of consumers to improve their financial lives and access what matters most. Leveraging innovative solutions that are shaping the future of retail commerce, Synchrony supports the growth and success of some of the nation's most respected brands, alongside hundreds of thousands of small and midsize businesses, including health and wellness providers. Committed to excellence in service and culture, Synchrony is honored to be ranked the #1 Best Company to Work For® in the U.S. by Fortune magazine and Great Place to Work®. For more information, visit www.synchrony.com . About Pet Resort Hospitality Group Pet Resort Hospitality Group (PRHG) is a provider of pet services, including daycare, boarding, grooming, and training. PRHG is led by a management team with decades of experience in the pet resort industry and a proven track record of successfully scaling consumer businesses. Many PRHG executives got their start as hourly employees caring for dogs. They worked their way up as independent owners before partnering with PRHG to further expand the potential for their services. Each business within the PRHG family benefits from the experience of the PRHG leadership team in areas such as acquisition planning and integration, growth planning and strategic tactics, brand and technology unification, scalable resources and support, and back office management. PRHG also recently launched Pet Resort University in Bentonville, Arkansas —a first of its kind educational center built by pet care professionals —to educate the next generation of pet resort managers, pet groomers, and dog trainers. This initiative showcases the company's commitment to advancing its employees and professionalizing the pet services industry. The Company is currently pursuing strategic add on acquisitions of pet services businesses throughout the United States. To learn more, visit www.petresorts.love . title: Alvotech Announces Closing of Public Offering and Full Exercise by Underwriters of Option to Purchase Additional Shares, Raising an Aggregate of $165 Million with Concurrent Private Placement
summary: REYKJAVIK, ICELAND (June 18, 2026) — Alvotech (NASDAQ: ALVO; ALVO-SDB) (“Alvotech” or the “Company”), a global biotechnology company specializing in the development and manufacture of biosimilar medicines for patients worldwide, today announced the closing on June 17, 2026 of its previously
body_text: REYKJAVIK, ICELAND (June 18, 2026) — Alvotech (NASDAQ: ALVO; ALVO-SDB) (“Alvotech” or the “Company”), a global biotechnology company specializing in the development and manufacture of biosimilar medicines for patients worldwide, today announced the closing on June 17, 2026 of its previously announced underwritten public offering (the “Offering”) of 26,066,667 of its ordinary shares at an offering price of $3.75 per share, which includes 3,400,000 ordinary shares issued pursuant to the exercise in full by the underwriters of their option to purchase additional ordinary shares in the Offering. All ordinary shares sold in the Offering were offered by Alvotech. Before deducting the underwriting discounts and commissions and offering expenses, the aggregate gross proceeds to the Company were approximately $98 million. Concurrent with the Offering, Alvotech entered into Subscription Agreements with certain investors that are professional clients or eligible counterparties in the European Economic Area falling within article 1(4) of Regulation (EU) 2017/1129, pursuant to which Alvotech will issue and sell 17,826,666 ordinary shares to such investors at a price of $3.75 per ordinary share, which represents the per share public offering price, in a private placement exempt from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. The gross proceeds from the concurrent private placement, before deducting any transaction-related expenses, are expected to be approximately $67 million. The concurrent private placement is expected to close on or about June 25, 2026, subject to customary conditions. The consummation of the Offering was not contingent on the consummation of the concurrent private placement. The board of directors of Alvotech has resolved to issue 43,893,333 ordinary shares to be delivered to investors participating in the Offering and the concurrent private placement and following closing of the concurrent private placement the issued share capital of Alvotech will amount to 390,431,480 ordinary shares in total. The total gross proceeds from the Offering, including gross proceeds from the underwriters’ exercise in full of their option to purchase additional shares, and the concurrent private placement are expected to be approximately $165 million, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses payable. Alvotech intends to use the net proceeds from this Offering and the concurrent private placement to fund the continued development of its biosimilar assets, as well as working capital and general corporate purposes, which may include, among others, intellectual property protection and enforcement, commercial expenditures, capital expenditures, acquisitions or collaborations, pre-clinical and clinical development of its product candidates, research and development and product development, pre-commercialization activities and repayment or refinancing of indebtedness or other corporate borrowings. BofA Securities, Jefferies and Evercore ISI acted as joint book-running managers for the Offering. The Offering was made pursuant to a registration statement on Form F-3, including a base prospectus, that was previously filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) on October 20, 2023, and declared effective on October 30, 2023. The ordinary shares referred to in this press release were offered in the United States only by means of a prospectus supplement and the accompanying prospectus that forms a part of the registration statement. Copies of the final prospectus supplement and the accompanying prospectus related to this Offering may be obtained from: BofA Securities, Attention: Prospectus Department, 201 North Tryon Street, Charlotte, NC 28255-0001, or by email at dg.prospectus_requests@bofa.com; Jefferies LLC, Attention: Equity Syndicate Prospectus Department, 520 Madison Avenue, New York, NY 10022, by telephone at (877) 821-7388, or by email at prospectus_department@jefferies.com; or Evercore Group L.L.C., Attention: Equity Capital Markets, 55 East 52nd Street, 35th Floor, New York, NY 10055, by telephone at (888) 474-0200, or by email at ecm.prospectus@evercore.com. Investors may also obtain these documents at no cost by visiting the SEC’s website at http://www.sec.gov . About Alvotech Alvotech is a biotechnology company, founded by Robert Wessman, focused solely on the development and manufacture of biosimilar medicines for patients worldwide. Alvotech seeks to be a global leader in biosimilars by delivering high-quality, cost-effective products and services, enabled by a fully integrated approach and broad in-house capabilities. Five biosimilars are already approved and marketed in multiple global markets, including biosimilars to Humira® (adalimumab), Stelara® (ustekinumab), Simponi® (golimumab), Eylea® (aflibercept) and Prolia®/Xgeva® (denosumab). The current development pipeline includes nine disclosed biosimilar candidates aimed at treating autoimmune disorders, eye disorders, osteoporosis, respiratory disease, and cancer. Alvotech has formed a network of strategic commercial partnerships to provide global reach and leverage local expertise in markets that include the United States, Europe, Japan, China, and other Asian countries and large parts of South America, Africa and the Middle East. title: Palo Alto Networks and Deutsche Telekom Bring AI-Driven Security with Advanced Sovereignty Controls for European Regulated Industries
summary: Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW) and Deutsche Telekom (XETRA: DTE) today announced Sovereign Cortex with T Security. This solution brings the Palo Alto Networks Cortex® AI-driven SecOps platform...
body_text: AMSTERDAM and MUNICH , June 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW) and Deutsche Telekom (XETRA: DTE) today announced Sovereign Cortex with T Security. This solution brings the Palo Alto Networks Cortex® AI-driven SecOps platform to Europe's most regulated industries, with data sovereignty controls independently governed by Deutsche Telekom. Today's AI-driven threat landscape demands immediate, real time effective cybersecurity. Yet many of Europe's regulated organisations – in healthcare, the public sector, financial services and critical national infrastructure – face a fundamental challenge: adopting cloud-delivered AI security, while meeting Europe's growing sovereignty requirements. Increasingly codified in GDPR, NIS2 and DORA and equivalent European frameworks, these requirements demand demonstrable controls that go beyond data residency: control over who can access data, how it is encrypted, how provider access is audited, and how it is handled in support operations. Sovereign Cortex with T Security addresses these requirements and enables Europe's most regulated organisations to adopt cloud-delivered security without sovereignty compromise. Anchored by Deutsche Telekom, as the independent European trust partner, it delivers the full capabilities of the Cortex platform with purpose-built sovereignty controls for Europe's regulatory environment. In addition to the data residency controls we provide customers for all of our cloud services, Sovereign Cortex with T Security provides additional sovereign controls for every layer of the environment. This includes customer and systems (telemetry) data, encryption keys, and independently audited access logs. Furthermore, all support personnel are based exclusively in Europe, and all contractual agreements are governed by European law. Helmut Reisinger, CEO of EMEA at Palo Alto Networks "European organisations — from public authorities to critical infrastructure operators — have been clear with us: they need real time AI-driven security and they need verifiable data sovereignty controls, and they should not have to choose between them. This is our direct response to what customers and regulators across Europe have been asking for – a service that honours Europe's sovereignty, maintains the security effectiveness and modular platformization our customers depend on, and reflects the trust they place in us." Thomas Tschersich, CEO Deutsche Telekom Security GmbH and CSO Deutsche Telekom AG "Our joint offering is currently unique in Europe at this level of quality. We meet the compliance requirements of NIS2, DORA, and KRITIS with respect to data sovereignty — without asking our customers to compromise on the effectiveness of their cyber defence." A customer-led approach to sovereignty This solution reflects direct engagement with regulated organisations and public authorities across Europe — designed around the specific, verifiable controls they require, not a broad interpretation of sovereignty. It is built to evolve as sovereignty regulation across Europe develops. Sovereign Cortex with T Security will initially be available to organisations in healthcare, financial services, the public sector and critical national infrastructure, with broader availability to follow. The initial release is planned for Q3 2026. Learn more about how Palo Alto Networks and Deutsche Telekom are bringing AI-driven security to European industries. About Palo Alto Networks Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW), the global AI cybersecurity leader, protects our digital way of life with a comprehensive portfolio of cybersecurity solutions and platforms across Network, Cloud, Security Operations, AI and Identity. Trusted by 70,000+ customers and powered by Unit 42 threat intelligence, our AI-driven platforms eliminate complexity, empowering enterprises to modernize with confidence and securing the speed of innovation. Explore the future of security at www.paloaltonetworks.com . About Deutsche Telekom Deutsche Telekom (XETRA:DTE) is Europe's leading digital telco company, serving around 220 million customers across mobile, fixed-network and IT services. Through its subsidiaries Deutsche Telekom Security and T-Systems, the Group is also one of Europe's largest providers of cybersecurity and managed security services. With security operations centers across Europe, an end-to-end European network and IT infrastructure, and decades of experience serving regulated industries and public-sector customers, Deutsche Telekom provides the European trust anchor for sovereign digital services. Learn more at www.telekom.com/companyprofile . title: Zoom CX at CCW 2026: New AI contact center tools for visibility, resolution, and ROI
summary: Zoom CX showcased Agent Architect, AI Expert Assist 3.0, and the Agent Performance Suite at CCW Las Vegas 2026. Here's what it means for contact center leaders.
body_text: At CCW Las Vegas 2026, Zoom CX delivered a clear message to contact center and customer experience leaders: deploying AI is only the beginning. The real challenge is visibility: knowing whether AI is working, where it's failing, and how to improve it. In this blog, we'll explore the latest innovations from Zoom CX, including what launched this week at Customer Contact Week (CCW), and real customer outcomes proving the platform story. What is Zoom CX? Zoom CX is Zoom's contact center and customer experience platform, bringing together Zoom Virtual Agent (AI-powered self-service), Zoom Contact Center (omnichannel routing and agent desktop), AI Expert Assist , CX Insights, Workforce Management and Quality Management into a single, unified system. Unlike point solutions that require separate vendors for automation, analytics, and compliance, Zoom CX brings each layer of the contact center onto one platform, with one customer data model, one agent desktop, and one administrative layer. The big idea: "Deployed isn't done" at CCW 2026 One of the most anticipated sessions at CCW 2026 was a fireside chat with Kentis Gopalla , Head of Product for WEM and the ZCX Ecosystem. Gopalla tackled the question on everyone's mind: you bought the platform, you ran the pilot, you presented the business case. So why are customers still repeating themselves, agents still drowning in wrap-up work, and leadership still asking where the ROI is? His message was clear: deploying AI is not the finish line. It's the starting line. "You don't have an AI problem. You have a visibility problem. The data to improve your customer outcomes already exists inside your conversations, your operations, your workforce metrics. The question is whether you're using it." Kentis Gopalla, Head of Product for WEM and the ZCX Ecosystem Systems built for isolated interactions often lack shared memory, persistent context, and a clear path to resolution. Gopalla identified four stages where AI investment stalls: No data to work with: Point solutions give one slice of the picture. Without a unified data model, AI has nothing meaningful to act on. Data locked in silos: The data exists across systems, but fragmented stacks mean it can't be acted on in real time. No insights tool: Data alone isn't enough. You need something that surfaces patterns and signals, not just exports and reports. No feedback loop: If findings never route back into AI systems, coaching queues, or knowledge bases, the loop never closes. Gopalla then laid out a practical framework for closing the gap: drive self-service resolution, optimize in real time, and close the loop with insights. The goal isn't managing more conversations. It's completing them. Zoom CX is built to deliver with persistent context across every channel and less behind-the-scenes friction burning out agents. Build better AI agents, faster: Agent Architect Announced on June 22, Agent Architect is Zoom Virtual Agent's new AI-powered agent creation tool. Agent Architect lets you create production-ready voice and digital AI agents from a single prompt. No workflow expertise needed. Just describe what you want the agent to do, and it handles the rest: interpreting your intent, filling in the gaps, connecting the right data sources, and generating a deployable workflow in minutes. What makes it different from a basic builder is how the agents actually work. Agents created with Agent Architect can reason through requests, collaborate with other agents, and orchestrate interactions across systems and channels, not just follow a script. For CX teams that have been stuck in planning mode, this removes the biggest bottleneck. Less time building means more time improving. See what's new in Zoom Virtual Agent Learn more Scale your human agents with AI Expert Assist 3.0 Zoom Contact Center's AI Expert Assist 3.0 is a hybrid agentic and intent-based system: a meaningful step beyond classic intent-only tools that surface suggestions without acting on them. Four capabilities define this release: Smart orchestration. When an agent handles a complex interaction with guidance coming from multiple sources, Smart Orchestration consolidates that guidance into a single, unified action path. Agents get one clear next step, not a list of competing suggestions. Workflow automation. AI Expert Assist can now complete multi-step tasks in third-party systems — with human approval required before execution: CRM updates, order lookups, and case creation on the agent's behalf. Agents review and confirm before the system acts, keeping humans in the decision loop while eliminating repetitive task work. Redesigned Expert Assist Agent Builder. The configuration interface has been rebuilt around guided, generative prompt-driven setup. Building a new Expert Assist workflow that previously took weeks now takes minutes. Agent tracing. Every AI action within Expert Assist generates an auditable record: what the AI reasoned, which tools it used, and what decision it reached. Agent Tracing gives supervisors and compliance teams the visibility they need to trust that AI is working as intended, and to identify and correct it when it isn't. Live AI interpreter: Zoom Contact Center now supports bi-directional simultaneous interpretation, natively built into the platform. It works across both voice and digital channels, eliminating language as a constraint on which agents can handle which customers. Chris Morrissey on Zoom's AI-native contact center vision General Manager of Zoom CX, Chris Morrissey, sat down with CX Today for an on-site video interview at CCW. The conversation covered Zoom's AI-native approach to the contact center, and why a unified platform produces fundamentally different outcomes than a stack of point solutions. The interview covered five themes: AI that is native, not bolted on. It's not about the number of AI features on a product sheet. It's whether AI is embedded natively across the full contact center stack , so automation, agent assist, analytics, and compliance all share the same data model and can act on context that siloed tools can't see. Outcomes over features. The conversation was anchored in measurable results, not positioning. Resolution rates, containment, CSAT, and cost per interaction were the benchmarks, not feature counts. The unified agent experience. Most agents are still tabbing between multiple windows in their contact center. When Zoom Virtual Agent escalates to a live agent, the full customer context (issue type, prior interactions, sentiment signals) travels with it, with no reintroduction and no data handoff gap. Human-first AI. Human oversight is a design principle in every AI capability Zoom ships. AI is built to assist and elevate agents, not replace them: Workflow Automation requires human approval before executing tasks, and Agent Tracing gives supervisors a full audit trail of every AI decision. The tension CX leaders face. Boards want AI ROI, customers want to feel heard, and agents are asked to deliver both at once. Morrissey shared his perspective on where the line sits and what "human-first, AI-powered" actually means when the pressure is on. CX Today and Chris Morrissey at CCW Watch full interview What it all means for CX leaders in 2026 CCW 2026 made one thing clear: it is no longer a question of whether to use AI in your contact center. The real question is whether you have the visibility to know if that AI is actually working. That is the gap Zoom addressed directly at CCW this year. The four stages Kentis Gopalla outlined: no data, siloed data, no insights, no feedback loop. These were not abstract concepts. They were problems every leader in that room recognized from their own organization. And each announcement Zoom made was a direct, product-by-product response to one of those gaps. Zoom CX now offers outcome-based pricing, aligning cost directly to the result customers are actually purchasing: resolution. You pay when the AI resolves the issue (specific pricing terms, conditions, and eligibility vary — contact your Zoom representative for details) . That shift moves the conversation away from feature evaluation and toward outcome accountability. It also reflects how Zoom is thinking about its own responsibility to customer results going forward . For CX leaders mapping out their AI roadmap, Zoom's CCW 2026 presence gives a useful frame: look for the platform that does not just deploy AI , but gives you the tools to know it is working, improve it continuously, and prove the results to your organization. Explore how Zoom CX supports your contact center goals Learn more Zoom CX FAQ What is Zoom CX and what does it include? Zoom CX is a contact center and customer experience platform that brings AI-powered self-service, omnichannel routing, agent assistance, operational analytics, and workforce engagement management together under one platform. Rather than requiring separate vendors for each layer of the contact center stack, Zoom CX runs automation, agent desktop, quality management, compliance, and insights on a shared data model and administrative layer. The platform includes Zoom Virtual Agent for AI-powered self-service; Zoom Contact Center for omnichannel routing and the agent desktop; AI Expert Assist for real-time agent guidance and workflow automation; CX Insights for operational intelligence; and Zoom Compliance Manager for regulated-industry archiving and governance. The unified architecture means every layer shares the same customer profile: context travels with the interaction from virtual agent to live agent without gaps. How does Zoom Virtual Agent's agent performance suite help contact centers improve over time? Agent performance suite gives contact center teams three feedback mechanisms that most AI deployments lack. Agent performance enables pre-deployment simulation and post-launch real-time dashboards tracking resolution rates, containment, CSAT, and cost per interaction. Quality management for Zoom Virtual Agent scores AI agent interactions continuously, surfacing where automation is falling short before failure compounds. Knowledge base (KB) suggestions extracts insights from escalated interactions that human agents resolved and recommends knowledge base updates, with human oversight applied before changes take effect. Together, these three capabilities create the feedback loop that converts a deployed AI agent into an improving one. Organizations can identify and address Virtual Agent gaps in near real time rather than waiting for a quarterly review. What does "outcome-based pricing" mean for Zoom Virtual Agent? Outcome-based pricing ties Zoom Virtual Agent's cost to resolved interactions rather than seat counts, channel fees, or per-minute consumption. Organizations pay when the AI successfully resolves a customer request, not for the infrastructure it runs on. For finance leaders evaluating AI ROI, outcome-based pricing converts the investment from a fixed platform cost to a variable cost that scales with successful resolution. It also changes the vendor relationship: Zoom's commercial interest is aligned to making the AI work better because better resolution rates directly affect per-interaction cost. How does Zoom CX handle AI quality and human oversight? Every AI capability in Zoom CX is designed with human oversight as an explicit architectural principle. Workflow automation in AI Expert Assist completes multi-step tasks in third-party systems but requires human approval before execution. Agent tracing generates auditable records of AI reasoning, tool usage, and decision flow, giving supervisors and compliance teams the ability to review and correct AI behavior. KB suggestions applies recommended knowledge base updates only after human review. Quality management for Zoom Virtual Agent scores AI interactions and surfaces issues to supervisors rather than applying fixes autonomously. The principle is consistent across the platform: AI handles the work that benefits from automation; humans retain oversight over decisions that carry consequence. What is CX Insights and how is it different from standard contact center reporting? CX Insights is Zoom Contact Center's conversational intelligence and operational analytics layer, designed to replace manual reporting workflows: weekly spreadsheet exports, end-of-week coaching reviews, and static dashboards that show what happened but not why. The practical difference is interaction speed and context. A supervisor who sees a CSAT dip can click on that signal and CX Insights automatically scopes the relevant transcripts and opens an investigation, with no export, no filter setup, and no waiting. Memory learns team structures, KPI definitions, and investigation patterns over time, enabling the platform to provide increasingly relevant insights as it accumulates organizational context. What is Agent Architect? Agent Architect is a prompt-driven creation tool in Zoom Virtual Agent that lets teams build production-ready AI agents from a single description. It automatically interprets intent, connects data sources, and generates deployable workflows in minutes. Unlike standard builders, Agent Architect uses reasoning and orchestration to create agents that can collaborate and act across systems , not just follow scripts. What is the Agent Performance Suite? The Agent Performance Suite is a performance optimization layer for Zoom Virtual Agent that tracks resolution rates, containment, and customer satisfaction across every interaction. It combines real-time dashboards, quality management, and continuous learning to help organizations measure and improve both virtual and human agent performance. What's new in AI Expert Assist 3.0? AI Expert Assist 3.0 introduces agentic task execution, allowing AI to not only suggest actions but complete them with agent approval. It consolidates guidance from multiple sources into a single action path, generates automatic interaction summaries, and provides real-time coaching insights, helping live agents work faster and with more consistent, relevant guidance.
