title: Park Dental Partners Affiliates Named "Minnesota’s Best" for the Sixth Year in a Row | Park Dental
summary: Park Dental Partners is pleased to announce the readers of the The Minnesota Star Tribune voted Park Dental and The Dental Specialists to the newspaper’s Minnesota’s Best list for a sixth consecutive year. Park Dental was voted “Minnesota’s Best” once again, earning the Readers’ Choice Gold Award in the General Dentistry – Multiple Locations category Read more...
body_text: Park Dental Partners is pleased to announce the readers of the The Minnesota Star Tribune voted Park Dental and The Dental Specialists to the newspaper’s Minnesota’s Best list for a sixth consecutive year. Park Dental was voted “Minnesota’s Best” once again, earning the Readers’ Choice Gold Award in the General Dentistry – Multiple Locations category for the sixth consecutive year. Park Dental has held the Readers’ Choice Gold Award ever since the Minnesota’s Best recognition program started in 2021. “Congratulations to all our Park Dental doctors and team members for their continuing commitment to quality, patient-centered care,” said Dr. Chris Steele, Park Dental Partners Chief Clinical Officer, General Practices. “While we have internal processes to evaluate patient satisfaction like the Press Ganey patient survey, it’s rewarding to see Park Dental come out on top of a more organic poll like this. It’s truly impressive to see the organization recognized year after year, which speaks to the consistency and high standards accomplished by everyone. The work our doctors and team members do every day makes a significant impact on patients’ lives, and the Minnesota’s Best poll bears that out.” The Dental Specialists earned the Readers’ Choice Gold Awards in the Oral Surgery and Orthodontics categories and the Silver Award in Pediatric Dentistry . The Dental Specialists Oral & Maxillofacial Surgeons have held the Readers’ Choice Gold Award for six consecutive years, an impressive accomplishment in the competitive specialty dentistry environment. The Dental Specialists Orthodontics and The Dental Specialists Pediatric Dentistry have also each earned a place on the Minnesota’s Best List for the past 6 years. Our Orthodontics team earned the Gold Award this year and in 2021 along with the Silver award from 2022 – 2025. The Dental Specialists Pediatric Dentistry has earned the Readers’ Choice Silver Award for six consecutive years. “I couldn’t be more pleased for our doctors and team members to receive this recognition,” said Dr. Alan Law, Park Dental Partners Chief Clinical Officer, Specialty Practices. “And to receive top recognition in three incredibly competitive specialties is amazing. It’s so gratifying to see that our patients take the time to weigh in on this poll. I don’t think we could ask for a better acknowledgement of the job we’re doing than this strong vote of confidence in the care our doctors and team members provide.” The newspaper polled readers on who they thought was “Minnesota’s Best.” Over one million votes were cast and more than 770 businesses were chosen in over 380 different categories, including professional services, restaurants, health and wellness. Voting took place earlier this year, with results published in a special section of The Minnesota Star Tribune Sunday, June 28 print edition and online at MinnesotasBest.com .

title: South Plains Financial, Inc. Announces Executive Leadership Transition
summary: ~ Curtis Griffith to Retire as Chief Executive Officer, Continue as Chairman of the Board ~ ~ Cory Newsom Appointed Chief Executive Officer Effective December 31, 2026 ~ LUBBOCK, Texas, June 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- South Plains Financial, Inc. (NASDAQ:SPFI) (“South Plains” or the “Company”),
body_text: PDF Version ~ Curtis Griffith to Retire as Chief Executive Officer, Continue as Chairman of the Board ~ ~ Cory Newsom Appointed Chief Executive Officer Effective December 31, 2026 ~ LUBBOCK, Texas, June 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- South Plains Financial, Inc. (NASDAQ:SPFI) (“South Plains” or the “Company”), the parent company of City Bank (“City Bank” or the “Bank”), today announced the upcoming retirement of Curtis Griffith, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, to be effective December 31, 2026. Mr. Griffith will remain a director of the Company and its wholly owned subsidiary, City Bank, and will continue to serve as Chairman of the Board. South Plains’ board of directors has appointed Cory Newsom, director and President, as the Company’s Chief Executive Officer, effective upon Mr. Griffith’s retirement on December 31, 2026. Curtis Griffith commented, “It has been the privilege of a lifetime to be part of building South Plains over more than four decades. What I am most proud of is the culture we’ve created—one centered on relationships and a shared commitment to helping people succeed. From our employees to our customers, partners and communities, we have always believed that our core purpose is to use the power of relationships to help people succeed and live better.” Mr. Griffith continued, “Our leadership transition has been the result of many years of deliberate planning, and Cory has been instrumental throughout that process. He has been leading our day-to-day operations and driving our growth strategy, with a clear focus on disciplined organic loan growth and strategic M&A, including the recent successful acquisition and integration of Bank of Houston. Cory’s leadership and execution give me confidence that this transition will be seamless and that South Plains will continue to deliver on its growth strategy and create long-term shareholder value.” Cory Newsom added, “I am honored to step into this role and grateful to our board for the opportunity to continue to be part of South Plains’ journey. Curtis’ leadership, partnership and unwavering commitment to our culture and communities have shaped this Company in a way that will endure, and I have learned a great deal working alongside him.” Mr. Newsom concluded, “As we look ahead, we will continue to execute on the strategy that has driven our success—expanding our lending platform, investing in experienced bankers, and pursuing disciplined, thoughtful growth opportunities—while maintaining the credit culture and relationship-based approach that has defined South Plains. The progress we have made in recent years provides a strong foundation, and I am excited to lead our team as we continue to build on that success.” To facilitate a smooth transition of the day-to-day leadership of the Company, the Company and the Bank have also entered into a Retirement and Consultancy Agreement with Mr. Griffith, pursuant to which Mr. Griffith will serve as a consultant to the Company beginning upon his retirement on December 31, 2026. title: E-Way Bill vs E-Invoice: Key Differences, Applicability & Examples
summary: Learn the difference between E-Way Bill and E-Invoice, their applicability, key features, examples, and GST compliance requirements for businesses.
body_text: E-Way Bill vs E-Invoice: Key Differences, Applicability & Examples Every growing business shares one common goal, keeping operations smooth while staying compliant with GST regulations. In the world of GST, understanding E-invoices and E-Way Bills is an important part of achieving that balance. When it comes to GST compliance, E-invoices and E-Way Bills are two important requirements businesses should understand. This often creates a dilemma for many businesses. Both of these documents are used during business transactions for GST compliance, and in some cases, a business may even need both for the same sale. Also, many people think both documents serve the same purpose, but they are used for quite different purposes. An E-Invoice helps businesses digitally authenticate invoice details under GST, while an E-way Bill helps for tracking purposes when goods are being transported from one location to another. Imagine, a business selling goods to a customer in another state, the business may need to generate an e-invoice for the transaction and an E-Way Bill before transporting the goods. Missing either document can cause compliance issues, delays, or even heavy penalties which every business should understand. To make things easier, we will explain E-Way Bill vs E-Invoice, their key differences, applicability, & real-life examples without any technical jargon. What is an E-Invoice An E-Invoice is a digital invoice system introduced under GST to make business transactions more transparent and easier to track. This does not mean businesses have to create invoices from scratch. Instead, businesses can continue to use their existing billing or accounting software and upload invoice details to the Invoice Registration Portal, or IRP. The portal then verifies the details and generates an IRN and QR code. This confirms that the invoice is valid under GST. The main purpose of an E-Invoice is to reduce manual errors, improve GST reporting, and create a standard process for invoice verification. ‍ Key Features of E-Invoice: Invoice details are registered electronically Generates a unique IRN number Includes a QR code for verification Help reduce mistakes in invoice reporting Making GST compliance easier for businesses What is an E-Way Bill An E-Way Bill is a digital document required for the movement of goods from one location to another under GST. It mentions goods, supplier, recipient, transporter, and vehicle used for transportation. The main purpose of an E-Way Bill is to keep a record of the movement of goods and ensure GST rules are being followed during transportation. Businesses and transporters must generate an E-Way Bill before goods movement when the value of the consignment exceeds the prescribed limit. Key Features of E-Way Bill: Track the movement of goods Required during transportation Contains vehicle and transporter details Helps GST authorities verify shipments Reduces paperwork during transit E-Way Bill vs E-Invoice: Key Differences Although both documents are linked with GST but they have different roles and by knowing how they differ helps businesses use the right document at the right time. Difference E-Invoice E-Way Bill Main purpose Invoice verification Goods movement tracking Related to Sales transaction Transportation of goods Generated by Supplier Supplier, recipient, or transporter Generated on Invoice Registration Portal E-Way Bill Portal Required before Issuing invoice Moving goods Includes Invoice and tax details Goods and transport details QR Code Available Not applicable Difference Between E-Invoice and E-Way Bill with Example Let us understand the difference more clearly. Assume that a business in Delhi sells machinery of ₹5 lakh to a customer in Punjab. Step 1: Generate E-Invoice The seller prepares the GST invoice and uploads the invoice details on the IRP portal. After checking the details, the system generates an IRN and QR code. This confirms that the invoice has been successfully registered under GST. Step 2: Generate E-Way Bill As the machinery is being shipped from Delhi to Punjab. A business has to create an E-Way Bill before the transportation begins. This helps track the movement of goods and ensures they can be transported as per GST rules. In this case: E-invoice to prove the transaction E-Way Bill allows legal movement of goods Applicability of E-Invoice E-Invoice applicability depends on the turnover limit and business category notified by the government. Generally, registered businesses crossing the specified turnover limit must generate e-invoices for their B2B transactions, exports, and other applicable supplies. Businesses should regularly check the latest updates on the official GST portal for applicable turnover limits and exemptions. Applicability of E-Way Bill An E-Way Bill is mostly required for the movement of goods when their value crosses the prescribed set value. It may be required for: Interstate movement of goods Intrastate movement as per state rules Supply of goods Goods sent for reasons other than supply Returns of goods An E-Way Bill is usually required before the transportation of goods begins. Benefits of E-Invoice Businesses can experience several advantages after adopting E-Invoicing: 1. Faster Invoice Processing Digital invoice verification reduces manual checking and speeds up business processes. 2. Lower Chances of Errors Automatic validation helps prevent mistakes in GST invoice details. 3. Easier GST Compliance Invoice data can be automatically shared with GST systems, making return filing easier. 4. Better Record Management Businesses can maintain digital invoice records without depending on physical paperwork. Make e-invoicing simpler with Swipe. Get started today for free and manage your GST invoices more efficiently. Benefits of E-Way Bill E-Way Bills provide several benefits to businesses involved in transportation: 1. Smooth Goods Movement Transporters can carry goods with proper digital documentation. 2. Reduced Documentation Businesses no longer need multiple physical documents during transportation. 3. Better Tracking Businesses can track shipment details and avoid unnecessary delays. 4. Improved GST Compliance Proper E-Way Bill generation helps businesses follow GST transportation rules. Can E-Invoice and E-Way Bill be Generated Together? Yes, businesses can generate both documents together. Many accounting and ERP systems allow businesses to generate an E-Way Bill using the details already available in the E-Invoice. This reduces repetitive data entry and helps save time. For example: A wholesaler selling products to another state can generate: GST Invoice E-Invoice with IRN and QR code E-Way Bill for transportation All three documents work together to complete the transaction smoothly. Common Mistakes Businesses Should Avoid Even small mistakes can create compliance challenges for businesses. We have given here some common ones: Generate E-Way Bill after goods have already moved Entering incorrect invoice details Using expired E-Way Bills Not updating vehicle details Ignoring GST portal updates ‍ Automated GST software can help minimize manual errors while also helping businesses stay on top of GST compliance rules. E-Way Bill vs E-Invoice: Quick Comparison Table Feature E-Invoice E-Way Bill Objective Validate invoices Track goods movement Related to Sales transactions Transporation Required For Eligible taxpayers Goods movement above limit Generated On IRP Portal E-Way Bill Portal QR Code Yes No Vehicle Details Not required Required Conclusion Hopefully, by now you have a clear picture of both of these documents. You may now have a better understanding of when each document is used and how they support GST compliance. While E-Invoice focuses on verifying invoice details, E-Way Bill helps track the movement of goods. Together they help businesses manage GST compliance with ease. Digital tools make these tasks a lot easier by automation, help reduce mistakes, and saving you time. Businesses can simplify invoicing, billing, and manage GST-related tasks more effortlessly with Swipe. Generate E-Invoices and E-Way Bills effortlessly with Swipe FAQs 1. Is E-Invoice the same as E-Way Bill? No, an E-Invoice validates a business transaction under GST, however an E-Way Bill helps track the movement of goods. 2. Is E-Way Bill required after generating an E-Invoice? Yes, if the goods are being transported and the conditions for E-Way Bill apply, businesses must generate it separately. 3. Who needs to generate an e-invoice? Businesses covered under GST e-invoice rules need to generate E-invoices for applicable transactions. 4. Who can generate an E-Way Bill? The supplier, recipient, or transporter can generate an E-Way Bill depending on the transaction. 5. What happens if goods are moved without an E-Way Bill? Failure to generate the required E-Way Bill can result in penalties and may also result in goods also being stopped during transportation. 6. Can E-Invoice and E-Way Bill be generated together? Indeed, many businesses generate both documents together through integrated billing and accounting systems. ‍

title: Daré Bioscience Announces the Upcoming Launch of Flora Sync LF5™ Vaginal Probiotic Capsules
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Daré Bioscience's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: First Product Revenue Expected This Month, Opening New Commercial Chapter for Women's Health Innovator Limited-Time Launch Offer: 30% Off + Free Shipping SAN DIEGO, June 04, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Daré Bioscience, Inc. (NASDAQ: DARE), a purpose-driven health biotech company solely focused on closing the gap in women's health between promising science and real-world solutions, today announced the upcoming commercial launch of Flora Sync LF5 ™, a vaginal probiotic capsule formulated specifically to restore microbiome balance and support lasting vaginal comfort. The launch represents a milestone for Daré, as the company expects to generate its first direct consumer product revenue in June 2026, marking the company's transition from a pure development-stage biotech to a women's health company with a revenue-generating product. Flora Sync LF5™ will be marketed under the brand family DARE to RESTORE™ and manufactured by Probiotical S.p.A., a global leader in probiotic development and manufacturing. "Flora Sync LF5 was developed specifically for vaginal health, not gut health," said Sabrina Martucci Johnson, President and Chief Executive Officer of Daré Bioscience. "By delivering a vagina-specific probiotic strain directly to the vaginal environment, Flora Sync LF5 represents a targeted approach to supporting vaginal wellness. This upcoming launch marks an important milestone for Daré as it represents the company’s first consumer health product launch. We continue to work to bring women other innovative, science-backed products they can access directly, without a prescription. We look forward to making Flora Sync LF5 available to women across the country and sharing our first commercial results with investors and our community." ABOUT FLORA SYNC LF5™ (DARE TO RESTORE™) Flora Sync LF5 is a targeted, non-hormonal probiotic vaginal capsule formulated with Limosilactobacillus fermentum LF5, a clinically studied probiotic strain originally isolated from the vaginal microbiome of healthy women with no reported history of yeast infections and backed by over 30 years of research. Unlike most probiotics marketed for vaginal health, which rely on gut strains taken orally, Flora Sync LF5 delivers a vagina-specific probiotic strain directly to the vaginal environment, where imbalance occurs. This targeted approach is designed to support a healthy vaginal microbiome, natural moisture balance, and overall vaginal wellness at the source. Flora Sync LF5 is manufactured by Probiotical S.p.A., a leader in probiotic science and manufacturing, under current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) standards. Probiotical oversees every step of the process, from strain selection and scientific validation through manufacturing and quality control, helping ensure product quality, consistency, purity, and performance. Upon launch, Flora Sync LF5 will be available without a prescription, for $49 per box (6 capsules), and offers a simple three-day routine designed for noticeable benefits. It is intended for women experiencing: Vaginal dryness leading to irritation or itching Unwanted odor or excess discharge Disruption following intimacy, hormonal shifts, or antibiotic use Routine changes such as travel, new products, or elevated stress CLINICALLY STUDIED. BACKED BY OVER 30 YEARS OF PROBIOTIC RESEARCH. Flora Sync LF5 is manufactured by Probiotical S.p.A., an Italian pioneer in probiotic science with roots in lactic acid bacteria research dating back nearly a century. From strain discovery and scientific validation to manufacturing under current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) standards, Probiotical maintains oversight of the entire process to deliver a high quality, clinically studied probiotic designed specifically for vaginal health. Flora Sync LF5 is supported by clinical research published in Frontiers in Microbiology (2024). In a single-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial of 100 women: 96% of women achieved vaginal microbiome balance within 3 days* 90% maintained a balanced vaginal microbiome at 2 weeks* *Based on a single-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial of 100 women published in Frontiers in Microbiology (2024) . Flora Sync LF5 is not intended to treat, cure, or prevent any disease or medical condition. LIMITED-TIME LAUNCH OFFER: GET 30% OFF + FREE SHIPPING To celebrate the upcoming launch of Flora Sync LF5 , Daré Bioscience is offering a limited-time promotion for women who sign up to receive launch updates. Women who register will receive a discount code for 30% off plus free shipping, redeemable when Flora Sync LF5 becomes available through the DARE Health Hub. This exclusive launch offer is designed to help more women experience a science-backed approach to vaginal wellness and to thank early supporters who have followed the product's development journey. A COMMERCIAL MILESTONE IN A PIPELINE BUILT FOR WOMEN The upcoming launch of Flora Sync LF5 marks the beginning of direct product revenue for Daré Bioscience, and arrives alongside significant momentum across the Company's broader pipeline. On May 18, 2026, Daré announced the initiation of its Phase 2 clinical study of DARE-HPV , a novel pharmacologic treatment for persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection — the leading cause of cervical cancer cases in the U.S. — with no currently U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved treatments. The Phase 2 study is a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in approximately 100 women. As previously announced, the study, as well as the broader DARE-HPV program, is funded by a $10 million contract funded by the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H). The Phase 2 study is expected to report topline data in 2027. On May 12, 2026, Daré announced positive interim safety and efficacy results from its ongoing Phase 3 study of Ovaprene ®, the Company's investigational monthly, hormone-free intravaginal contraceptive. The trial's independent Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) conducted a second planned interim analysis focused on reviewing safety data from the study, and recommended the study continue without modification, consistent with its recommendation from the first interim analysis in July 2025. There currently are no FDA-approved, hormone-free, monthly intravaginal contraceptives. Daré is also advancing DARE to PLAY™ Sildenafil Cream , a first-of-its-kind topical sildenafil cream for women, with dispensing through the DARE Health Hub targeted to commence this summer. "We are building a company that generates revenue and advances science at the same time," Ms. Johnson continued. "Flora Sync LF5 will be the first chapter in Daré's consumer revenue story, and we intend to keep building from here, for women, and for our investors." ABOUT DARÉ BIOSCIENCE, INC. Daré Bioscience (NASDAQ: DARE) is a purpose-driven health biotech company solely focused on closing the gap in women's health between promising science and real-world solutions. Every innovation Daré advances is based in advanced science and backed by rigorous, peer-reviewed research. From contraception to menopause, sexual health to fertility, vaginal health to infectious disease, Daré is working to close critical gaps in care using science that serves her needs. For decades, women have been told to "wait it out" or "live with it," while innovations that could improve their quality of life languish in the regulatory or funding pipeline. With growing awareness around menopause, sexual health, and vaginal health, the conversation is shifting. However, access to proven solutions is lagging. Daré is working to change that. Learn more at darebioscience.com . Introducing groups and access controls
summary: Groups and access controls let you decide exactly who can access what in Basedash. Bundle users into groups, grant each one access to the data sources,…
body_text: Today we’re launching groups and access controls in Basedash. Basedash is a BI tool the whole company touches — so who can see what really matters. Now you control it precisely. Create groups for the way your company actually works, grant each group access to exactly what it needs, and give every group its own AI context so the assistant behaves differently for different people. Why we built it Access and governance are the difference between a BI tool a few analysts use and one the whole company — plus the people outside it — can be trusted with. The moment you connect real data and point an AI analyst at it, the question stops being “can we answer this?” and becomes “who should be allowed to ask?” Groups and access controls answer that question. You decide who is in each group, what each group can reach, and how the AI talks to them. Group your users Bundle people into groups that match how you work — your data team, growth, leadership, or an external client you share dashboards with. Each group is a single place to manage everything those users can do. Add a person to a group and they inherit its access immediately. Remove them and it’s revoked just as fast. Grant access to anything This is the core of it: a group’s access covers everything in Basedash, not just dashboards. Toggle on exactly what a group should reach and leave the rest off. You can scope a group to specific: Data sources — choose which databases and warehouses a group can query Dashboards — share the right reports, and only those Chats — control who joins which conversations Automations — decide who receives each scheduled report MCP servers — grant tool access on a per-group basis So your external stakeholders can see their own client dashboard and nothing else, while your data team keeps full access to everything. Steer the AI per group Permissions decide what a group can reach. AI context decides how the assistant talks to them. Every group gets its own context that’s applied to every answer automatically. Tell the assistant something like “you’re talking to an external client, only reference their own account data, and keep explanations non-technical,” and every response for that group follows it — on top of the row-level security that already applies to every question. Same product, different behavior depending on who’s asking. Who gets what Because groups map to real teams and audiences, access falls out naturally — each group gets exactly the slice of Basedash it needs. How it works It’s three steps: group your users, grant the access each group needs, and steer how the AI answers for them. Set it once and it applies everywhere — chats, dashboards, automations, and the MCP server alike. Getting started Groups and access controls are available today for all Basedash users: Sign up for Basedash (or log in) and connect your data sources Open Settings → Groups and create a group for a team or audience Grant the group access to the data sources, dashboards, chats, and automations it needs Add an AI context so the assistant answers the way that group should hear it What’s next A BI tool is only as useful as it is trusted. Now the right people see the right data — and the AI knows who it’s talking to. Try groups and access controls today — control exactly who can access your data.
